newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy supports acceleration towards EMU - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy supports acceleration towards EMU - Prodi.

text.p: Italy would support an acceleration of the process towards Europe's single currency as a way to spur employment and economic development, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said this weekend.
"The earlier we decide on the Euro, the earlier will employment and development take off again," Prodi told reporters at a festival in this small town to celebrate his 58th birthday.

Prodi was commenting an interview he gave to the German weekly newspaper Welt am Sonntag in which he expressed worry that political paralysis in Germany was harming the planned launch of European monetary and economic union (EMU) in 1999.
Prodi reiterated that Italy would be ready at any time to join EMU.

"Italy has to be ready at any moment and I don't want Italy's timing to affect Europe's timing. We must be ready simply because the earlier we close this period of uncertainty, the better it is for all of us," Prodi said.

Earlier this week, Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy was ready to join the single currency and that the time had arrived to start discussions on an acceleration of the process towards EMU.

Ciampi said in an interview on Saturday, however, that despite a strong start to the year, Italy is not yet certain to meet its deficit goal for 1997 because the autumn months pose a potential threat to state accounts.

Italy has pledged to cut its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year from 6.7 percent in 1996, to meet a key criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to join the single currency.
